reticulumLocalInterfaces.offlineHintBle: To clear this error you may need to remove this interface and add it back (Pick device) so the saved Bluetooth id is refreshed, then restart the stack. Your OS may prompt for a 6-digit Bluetooth PIN (macOS, Windows, or Linux). RNode generates a new code each pairing — never use 123456 (that is Meshtastic’s default, not RNode). The RNode need not appear in System Settings → Bluetooth before this app connects; the OS dialog appears when the stack pairs. Headless radios: connect USB → Reticulum Admin → Bluetooth → Start pairing → enter the PIN shown in the Admin panel (not on the radio display) into the OS dialog. Radios with a display: hold the button ~7 s on Heltec devices (timing varies; ~10 s on many boards enables Wi-Fi AP instead), read the PIN on screen, then enter it in the OS dialog. Clear failed bonds in your OS Bluetooth settings before retrying.
reticulumLocalInterfaces.offlineHintBleBondStale: macOS still shows this RNode as Paired, but Bluetooth keys no longer match (Peer removed pairing information). reticulumLocalInterfaces.offlineHintWifi: Check that the RNode is on your LAN, powered on, and reachable at the configured IP (default TCP port 7633, not 4242). Update the host below if DHCP assigned a new address, or re-provision Wi-Fi in Reticulum → Admin.
reticulumLocalInterfaces.connectingHintBle: BLE RNode links can take up to 60 seconds after the stack starts (OS passkey window). Enter the current RNode PIN if prompted — never 123456. This is normal, not an error. The device may not appear in System Settings until after a successful bond.

reticulumSharedInstance.networkHint: Or open Network → Share Reticulum instance to turn Share off manually, then restart the stack. You can also fully quit MeshChat, Ratspeak, or standalone rnsd and restart.

reticulumSidecarIssues.tcpConnectFailed: {{name}}: TCP connection refused or timed out

reticulumSidecarIssues.tcpResetByPeer: {{name}}: hub reset the TCP session (Connection reset by peer)
reticulumSidecarIssues.tcpReadEof: {{name}}: hub closed TCP cleanly (INFO: TCP read: EOF)
reticulumSidecarIssues.txQueueDropsHint: Usually caused by a dead TCP interface still enabled. Disable unreachable hubs to stop queue overflow.
reticulumSidecarIssues.txQueueDropsHintBle: This BLE RNode cannot drain its TX queue (link stuck or flapping). Prefer USB serial or Wi-Fi (tcp://), or Stop stack and re-pair after Forget in System Settings → Bluetooth.
reticulumSidecarIssues.txQueueDropsHintBleBondStale: TX queue is full because the BLE bond is stale. Forget this RNode in System Settings → Bluetooth, then use Admin → Bluetooth (Clear paired / Start pairing) or switch to USB.
reticulumSidecarIssues.txQueueDropsHintBleFlowControl: Host TX queue backpressure while the radio is busy (flow control on). Expected under RF congestion — not a stuck link. Reduce outbound load or wait for airtime.
reticulumSidecarIssues.txQueueDropsHintNeutral: This interface TX channel is full. Check that interface’s link health (or disable it) to stop drops.
reticulumSidecarIssues.bleBondRemoved: {{name}}: Bluetooth bond is stale (OS still shows Paired)
reticulumSidecarIssues.bleBondRemovedHint: Forget this RNode in System Settings → Bluetooth first (macOS will not clear Paired automatically). Prefer USB serial or Wi-Fi (tcp://) when possible to avoid BLE bonds. Then: Admin → Bluetooth → Clear paired devices (USB, ESP32) if available, Start pairing, remove and re-add this BLE interface (Pick device), restart the stack, and enter the new 6-digit PIN.
reticulumSidecarIssues.blePairingTimedOutHint: Stop the stack, start pairing again (Admin → Bluetooth shows the PIN in the panel — the radio display may stay blank — or ~7 s button hold for an on-screen PIN), restart the stack once, and enter that PIN in the OS dialog within ~60 seconds. Never use 123456 (Meshtastic default).
reticulumSidecarIssues.transportSaturatedHint: Disable dead interfaces and restart the stack. Reduce concurrent Reticulum traffic.
reticulumSidecarIssues.slowTransportQuery: RNS transport queries slow or failing ({{count}}×)
reticulumSidecarIssues.slowTransportQueryHint: The sidecar transport actor may be wedged — restart the Reticulum stack.
reticulumSidecarIssues.shareInstanceHint: Share instance is enabled — fully quit other Reticulum apps (MeshChatX, Ratspeak, standalone rnsd) and restart this stack before retrying DMs.
reticulumSidecarIssues.suppressed: {{count}} similar sidecar log lines suppressed recently.

reticulumInterfaces.backboneEnableGuidanceLead: Enable 1 to 3 backbone gateways at most
reticulumInterfaces.backboneEnableGuidanceBody: —2 is the sweet spot for redundancy without unnecessary bandwidth bloat. Aim for 1 global hub and 1 regional gateway, and enable specialty interfaces (like I2P or Yggdrasil) strictly as needed. Locally connected RNodes and local LAN interfaces do not count toward this backbone limit.

reticulumInterfaces.rnodeWifiSetupHint:
Wi-Fi is off after flashing — provision the RNode first (Reticulum → Admin → Wi-Fi, or join its AP and open http://10.0.0.1). Requires ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi-capable firmware.

After station mode: find the IP on the OLED alternate screen, your router DHCP list, or Admin → Read config. Use tcp://host (default port 7633) — not the TCP Client interface type.

~10 s button hold on many Heltec boards enables Wi-Fi AP (~7 s is Bluetooth pairing).
reticulumInterfaces.modeHint: Controls how this interface joins the wider network (path seeking, announce propagation). On add, Type default is Boundary for TCP/UDP/I2P hubs and Access point for RNodes. On edit, Default (clear) omits mode (RNS Full).

modeDescriptions.full: Full mesh participation. Routes traffic and auto-propagates announces. Use for primary nodes and repeaters.
modeDescriptions.access_point: Quiet until queried. Short path expiry. Ideal for wide-area radios serving intermittent users.
modeDescriptions.roaming: Mobile interfaces. Short path timeouts and active discovery. Use for handheld or vehicular RNodes.
modeDescriptions.boundary: Network boundary. Bridges distinct segments while isolating local traffic. Use for Internet/LoRa links.
modeDescriptions.gateway: Path-seeking for clients. Resolves unknown destinations on behalf of connected nodes.
modeDescriptions.point_to_point: Direct link between two nodes. No routing or announce propagation.

nonLoraNoiseRfi.title: Locate non-LoRa interference
nonLoraNoiseRfi.description: Identify motors, monitors, or power electronics near the antenna; relocate antenna or source.

industrial900mhz.title: Avoid bursty 900MHz sources
industrial900mhz.description: Smart meters and industrial telemetry can spike the channel — antenna placement and shielding help.

channelUtilizationSpike.title: Check for surge in traffic or interference
channelUtilizationSpike.description: CU is well above recent average — temporary congestion or new interference; monitor and adjust hop limits if sustained.

meshCongestion.title: Reduce hop limit / check MQTT overlap
meshCongestion.description: High duplicate rate — see Diagnostics duplicate-traffic block; try Ignore MQTT for bridged nodes.

hiddenTerminalRisk.title: Improve geometry or reduce concurrency
hiddenTerminalRisk.description: Concurrent transmitters may not hear each other — fewer hops, better placement, or fewer simultaneous talkers.

loraCollisionCorruption.title: Filter band / relocate
loraCollisionCorruption.description: Non-Meshtastic LoRa or collisions — directional antenna or channel planning may help.

externalInterference.title: Identify dominant transmitter
externalInterference.description: Another transmitter is backing off your node — find and mitigate the source or relocate.

widebandNoiseFloor.title: Reduce broadband noise sources
widebandNoiseFloor.description: Faulty electronics and power-line noise raise the floor — isolate antenna from noise sources.

fringeWeakCoverage.title: Improve path or add relay
fringeWeakCoverage.description: Node is at edge of coverage — relay placement or antenna upgrade.

elevatedNoiseFloor.title: Identify and remove interference source
elevatedNoiseFloor.description: Elevated noise floor reduces range and SNR — check for nearby electronics, switching power supplies, or motors.

excessiveFlooding.title: Allow direct routes to establish
excessiveFlooding.description: Flood ratio is very high — wait for the node to accumulate direct-path contacts, or check repeater proximity.

highCompanionTxQueue.title: Reduce outbound traffic or check the RF link
highCompanionTxQueue.description: Companion TX queue is nearly full — pause sends, reduce floods, or check for interference and weak links.

flasher.title: RNode Firmware Flasher
flasher.noSerialPortsHint: Connect your board over USB. Bluetooth devices in the log are ignored; only USB serial ports can be used for flashing.
flasher.portContentionWarning: Stop the Reticulum stack or disable the active RNode serial interface before flashing. Disconnect Meshtastic or MeshCore serial on the same port.
flasher.stackStoppedHint: Reticulum stack is stopped — the serial port is free for flashing. Start the stack again on the Connection tab when you are done.
flasher.esp32BootHint: Use a data USB cable (not charge-only). Stop other apps using the same serial port before flashing.
flasher.enterDfuHint: For nRF52 boards: puts the device into USB DFU bootloader mode (1200 baud touch).
flasher.dfuModeDone: Device should now be in DFU mode.
flasher.provisionRequiresFlash: Flash firmware successfully before using this step.
flasher.provisionHint: Required for new devices after flashing. Writes device identity, checksum, and lock byte.
flasher.provisionAlreadyDone: EEPROM is already provisioned. Wipe it first to reprovision.
flasher.firmwareHashHint: Run after each firmware flash. Reads the target hash from the device and writes it to EEPROM.
flasher.firmwareHashRequiresProvision: Provision the EEPROM before setting the firmware hash.
flasher.firmwareHashNotProvisioned: EEPROM is not provisioned. Provision the device first.
flasher.wipeEepromConfirmMessage: This erases device provisioning and takes about 30 seconds. The device will reboot when finished.
flasher.bluetoothHint: Enable Bluetooth on the device, then use Start pairing. The 6-digit PIN appears in this panel over USB — the radio display often stays blank. Enter that PIN in your OS Bluetooth dialog when Reticulum connects over BLE. RNode has no default PIN (do not use 123456 — that is Meshtastic). On display boards, a ~7 s button hold can also show a PIN on screen. The RNode may not appear in System Settings → Bluetooth until after a successful bond. Clear paired devices (ESP32) clears the radio bond table over USB before re-pairing; you must still Forget the device in System Settings.
flasher.clearPairedDevicesConfirmMessage: This sends CMD_BT_UNPAIR over USB and clears bonded hosts on ESP32 RNodes (no-op on some nRF52 builds). You must still Forget the device in System Settings → Bluetooth before re-pairing.
flasher.pairingWaiting: Waiting for pairing PIN from the radio over USB…
flasher.pairingPinEnterHint: Enter this code in the OS Bluetooth dialog when the stack connects. Do not use 123456.
flasher.wifiHint: Wi-Fi is disabled after flashing. Configure station mode here (USB serial), then add a Wi-Fi RNode interface on Connection with tcp://host (port 7633). Requires ESP32-S3 Wi-Fi-capable firmware. Reboot the board after applying changes.
flasher.wifiOffSuccess: Wi-Fi disabled. Reboot the board for changes to take effect.
flasher.wifiApSuccess: Access point mode enabled. Join the RNode AP from your computer (default gateway 10.0.0.1), then configure station credentials or use the bootstrap console.
flasher.wifiStationSuccess: Station mode saved. Reboot the board, then find its IP (display, router DHCP, or Read config) and add tcp://… on Connection → Interfaces.
flasher.tncHint: KISS TNC over serial for amateur-radio apps. Leave disabled when using Reticulum or mesh chat clients.

ble-connection.label: BLE Connection Issues
ble-connection.recommendation: BLE connection unstable. Check distance to device and Bluetooth adapter status.

mqtt.label: MQTT Issues
mqtt.recommendation: MQTT connection issues. Verify broker URL, credentials, and network connectivity.

mqtt-retries-exhausted.label: MQTT Reconnect Limit
mqtt-retries-exhausted.recommendation: MQTT gave up after max reconnects. Confirm the broker is reachable, credentials and port are correct, and firewalls allow outbound traffic.

watchdog.label: Watchdog Triggers
watchdog.recommendation: Watchdog triggered reconnection. Device communication may be unstable.

handshake.label: Handshake Failures
handshake.recommendation: Connection handshake failed. Try reconnecting manually.

ble-connect-race.label: BLE Connect Race/Timeout
ble-connect-race.recommendation: BLE handshake timed out or raced with disconnect. Check BLE connection stability and distance to device.

auth-decrypt.label: Auth/Decryption Failures
auth-decrypt.recommendation: Authentication or decryption failure. Verify channel keys match between devices.

native-module.label: Native Module Load Failure
native-module.recommendation: A native add-on failed to load — often wrong Electron ABI after an upgrade. Run pnpm install in the project folder (or pnpm run rebuild), quit all app instances, and retry.

internal-error.label: Internal App Errors
internal-error.recommendation: An unexpected internal error occurred. Please report this bug with the log file.

database-error.label: Database Failures
database-error.recommendation: Database error. This may indicate a corrupt database file or permission issue.

database-chmod.label: Database chmod (non-fatal)
database-chmod.recommendation: Database file permission tweak failed (often benign on Windows). If you see real DB errors elsewhere, check antivirus and folder permissions for the mesh-client userData directory.

database-writable.label: Database Not Writable
database-writable.recommendation: The app cannot write its database folder. Fix permissions on the mesh-client userData directory (see troubleshooting: Database directory is not writable).

tak-server.label: TAK Server Issues
tak-server.recommendation: TAK server error. Check certificate status and port availability.

updater.label: App Updater Errors
updater.recommendation: App updater error. Check your internet connection or try a manual update from GitHub.

meshcore-tcp.label: MeshCore IP Bridge Errors
meshcore-tcp.recommendation: MeshCore TCP bridge error. Verify the remote host and port are reachable.

ble-meshcore-notify-watchdog.label: BLE Notify Watchdog (MeshCore)
ble-meshcore-notify-watchdog.recommendation: No GATT notify data within the watchdog window (common on Windows). Retry connect; ensure the radio is paired in OS Bluetooth settings before connecting.

bluetooth-pairing.label: Bluetooth Pairing Issues
bluetooth-pairing.recommendation: Bluetooth pairing or unpair failed, or the PIN prompt timed out. Open the app when pairing, enter the PIN promptly, check the MAC address and Bluetooth permissions, or remove and re-pair from OS Bluetooth settings.

store-forward.label: Store & Forward History Issues
store-forward.recommendation: Store & Forward chat history could not be requested from a router (often a brief race with other radio traffic). If chat backlog stays empty, reconnect or wait for the next router heartbeat.

sdk-meshtastic.label: Meshtastic SDK Warnings/Errors
sdk-meshtastic.recommendation: Meshtastic stack reported a warning or error. If it repeats, check firmware, transport (BLE/serial), and reconnect.

sdk-meshcore.label: MeshCore SDK Warnings/Errors
sdk-meshcore.recommendation: MeshCore stack reported a warning or error. If it repeats, check BLE pairing, MQTT settings, and reconnect.

reticulum-nomad-hosting.label: Nomad Page Hosting Issues
reticulum-nomad-hosting.recommendation: Nomad My Pages hosting failed or the content folder is unavailable. Open Nomad Network → My Pages, re-choose the pages folder if it moved, then Start serving. Details appear as [nomad-serving] / [NomadHosting] in the log.
